question: Will this person be interested in the app (Q21 = 4 or 5)?
columns_used: Q1-Q20 (everything asked before the intent question); target is Q21 as yes/no
verdict: Works well. AUC of 0.5 is guessing and 1.0 is perfect, so about 0.9 means the model ranks interested people far above uninterested ones.

question: Which customers are most, medium and least likely, and what are they like?
columns_used: Demographics, shopping habits, handmade buying, attitudes Q15, price belief, number of services wanted. Intent is left out and used only afterwards to rank the segments
metric: Silhouette at k=3 (best k in brackets) / stability vs hierarchical clustering (ARI)
verdict: Moderate. The three tiers differ a lot in interest (see profile table) but the borders are soft, so use them for targeting, not as hard rules.

question: If someone wants two services, will they also want a third?
metric: Rules found / strongest two-service rule with support of at least 8%
result: 229 rules / S1 + S9 -> S4: confidence 85.8%, lift 1.93
verdict: Works for bundling. Lift above 1 means the services are wanted together more often than chance. Rules with very low support are ignored.

question: How much will they pay per item (Q23)?
metric: Hold-out R-squared on log scale / average miss in INR
verdict: Good for ranking and segment averages, weaker for exact rupee values. A plain regression on raw values with outliers explains almost nothing.

question: How much will they spend on the app in a year (Q24)?
metric: Hold-out R-squared on log scale / average miss in INR
verdict: Intent (Q21) is by far the strongest driver. Predictions are rough because many people spend zero.
